description:
When an agent calls a scenario CLI or API and the scenario is unreachable, the agent currently gets a generic connection error. It cannot differentiate transient outage (wait and retry) from intentional stop (start it) from crashed (escalate, dont retry) from being-tested (wait without interfering). This forces every scenario-down event into expensive heuristic decisions or capability-gap raises that re-fire whenever the underlying scenario blips.

This research item scopes a foundational solution: scenarios surface a structured reason field on unavailability errors. Authoritative reasons only — never guess. Agents that handle the field become smarter; agents that ignore it still work. Backwards-compatible.

RESEARCH QUESTIONS:
1. State machine — what is the canonical set of reasons? Proposed seed: running, stopping, starting, restarting, stopped, crashed, testing, unknown. Validate against actual lifecycle states the projects-CLI core tracks today.
2. CLI Phase A design — projects-CLI core surfaces lifecycle state when a scenario CLI call fails. The data exists (vrooli scenario status already reports it); the question is the error-envelope shape and how every scenario CLI plumbs through it without bespoke per-scenario plumbing.
3. API Phase B design — for API-to-API communication via the shared discovery package, the calling scenarios API gets a TCP-level error and must ask discovery why. Two architectural options: (a) discovery maintains a state cache that scenarios consult; (b) discovery becomes authoritative about state. Evaluate trade-offs (latency, staleness, blast radius, complexity) and pick.
4. Scope boundary — should the classification cover transient errors mid-call (e.g., scenario crashed during a request) in addition to pre-call unavailability? Lean is yes for completeness, but scoping needs to be explicit.
5. ROI validation — review the last N capability-gap items where the root cause was scenario-was-unavailable. How many would have been auto-resolved or differently-shaped by classification? This number is the actual ROI estimate.
6. Suspected vs authoritative — the known design risk. Operator stance: only emit reason when authoritatively known; otherwise emit reason=unknown. Validate this stance with concrete failure scenarios.

DESIGN CONSTRAINTS (settled, not up for debate):
- Only authoritative reasons. unknown is a valid reason; never guess.
- Backwards-compatible. Agents that ignore the field continue to work.
- CLI Phase A must ship before API Phase B. Phase A is days of work; Phase B is weeks. Dont gate Phase A on Phase B.
- Composes with wrap-not-use. As scenarios become the substrate, scenario-availability classification becomes equivalent to HTTP status codes for the scenario layer. Foundational.

DELIVERABLE: a research conclusion document (per the research-backlog-rework convention) covering the proposed state machine, both phase designs, the suspected-vs-authoritative discipline, the ROI estimate from historical capability-gap analysis, and a recommendation on whether to proceed to execute items and in what order. Should also identify any prerequisite refactors in projects-CLI core or discovery package before execute is feasible.

SEED CONTEXT:
- Vision walk #4 (2026-04-27) first divergence — origin of this item; rejected dec-1777232213798487055 contains the rationale that surfaced this gap.
- oss-advertisers two original suggestions in dec-1777232213798487055 rationale: (a) supervisor restart on health-check failure, (b) lifecycle hook flagging long-idle stops as crashes. Both fall out of the broader classification layer.
- The wrap-not-use principle (project memory project_wrap_not_use_principle.md) is the architectural frame this item operates within.

title: Research: Scenario availability classification (structured error reasons across CLI + API)
